certificate_policy: Each closed certificate was reconstructed from its script, packages each declared dependency as a self-contained checked Cut node, and passed the independent kernel from the empty context. Cut nodes contain their proposition and both proof branches; they do not refer to an external theorem environment, theorem name, or certificate hash.

theorems.name: zero_add
theorems.statement: forall n. 0 + n = n
theorems.summary: Zero is a left identity for addition; unlike PA3, this needs induction.

theorems.name: add_succ_left
theorems.statement: forall n m. S n + m = S (n + m)
theorems.summary: A successor can move through addition on the left.

theorems.name: add_comm
theorems.statement: forall n m. n + m = m + n
theorems.summary: Addition is commutative.

theorems.name: add_assoc
theorems.statement: forall n m k. (n + m) + k = n + (m + k)
theorems.summary: Addition is associative.

theorems.name: mul_zero_left
theorems.statement: forall n. 0 * n = 0
theorems.summary: Zero annihilates multiplication on the left.

theorems.name: mul_succ_left
theorems.statement: forall n m. S n * m = n * m + m
theorems.summary: A successor can move through multiplication on the left.

theorems.name: mul_comm
theorems.statement: forall n m. n * m = m * n
theorems.summary: Multiplication is commutative.

theorems.name: mul_add
theorems.statement: forall n m k. n * (m + k) = n * m + n * k
theorems.summary: Multiplication distributes over addition on the right.

theorems.name: mul_assoc
theorems.statement: forall n m k. (n * m) * k = n * (m * k)
theorems.summary: Multiplication is associative.

theorems.name: one_mul
theorems.statement: forall n. 1 * n = n
theorems.summary: One is a left identity for multiplication.

theorems.name: mul_one
theorems.statement: forall n. n * 1 = n
theorems.summary: One is a right identity for multiplication.

theorems.name: add_mul
theorems.statement: forall n m k. (n + m) * k = n * k + m * k
theorems.summary: Multiplication distributes over addition on the left.

theorems.name: succ_ne_zero
theorems.statement: forall n. ~(S n = 0)
theorems.summary: No successor is zero (the reusable PA1 lemma).

theorems.name: succ_injective
theorems.statement: forall n m. S n = S m -> n = m
theorems.summary: Successor is injective (the reusable PA2 lemma).

theorems.name: le_refl
theorems.statement: forall n. n <= n
theorems.summary: The defined order is reflexive; zero is its witness.

theorems.name: le_trans
theorems.statement: forall n m k. n <= m -> m <= k -> n <= k
theorems.summary: Order witnesses compose by addition, so the defined order is transitive.

theorems.name: no_succ_add_fixed
theorems.statement: forall p n. S p + n = n -> false
theorems.summary: Adding a positive successor cannot leave a natural number fixed.

theorems.name: drop_add_prefix_from_fixed
theorems.statement: forall a b n. (b + a) + n = n -> a + n = n
theorems.summary: A fixed-point equation remains fixed after dropping an additive prefix.

theorems.name: antisymm_from_witnesses
theorems.statement: forall a b n m. a + n = m -> b + m = n -> n = m
theorems.summary: Opposing additive witnesses force equality.

theorems.name: le_antisymm
theorems.statement: forall n m. n <= m -> m <= n -> n = m
theorems.summary: The witness-defined order is antisymmetric.

theorems.name: le_total
theorems.statement: forall n m. n <= m \/ m <= n
theorems.summary: Every pair of natural numbers is comparable in the defined order.

theorems.name: add_eq_zero_right
theorems.statement: forall a b. a + b = 0 -> b = 0
theorems.summary: A sum equal to zero has zero as its right addend.

theorems.name: mul_eq_zero
theorems.statement: forall n m. n * m = 0 -> n = 0 \/ m = 0
theorems.summary: Zero products have a zero factor: the 23-entry core capstone.

theorems.name: eq_symm
theorems.statement: forall a b. a = b -> b = a
theorems.summary: Equality is symmetric.

theorems.name: eq_trans
theorems.statement: forall a b c. a = b -> b = c -> a = c
theorems.summary: Equality is transitive.

theorems.name: succ_congr
theorems.statement: forall a b. a = b -> S a = S b
theorems.summary: Successor preserves equality.

theorems.name: zero_or_succ
theorems.statement: forall n. n = 0 \/ exists k. n = S k
theorems.summary: Every natural is either zero or the successor of a natural.

theorems.name: nonzero_is_succ
theorems.statement: forall n. ~(n = 0) -> exists k. n = S k
theorems.summary: Every nonzero natural has a predecessor.

theorems.name: add_congr
theorems.statement: forall a b c d. a = b -> c = d -> a + c = b + d
theorems.summary: Addition preserves equality in both arguments.

theorems.name: mul_congr
theorems.statement: forall a b c d. a = b -> c = d -> a * c = b * d
theorems.summary: Multiplication preserves equality in both arguments.

theorems.name: add_right_cancel
theorems.statement: forall a b c. a + c = b + c -> a = b
theorems.summary: A common right addend can be cancelled.

theorems.name: add_left_cancel
theorems.statement: forall a b c. a + b = a + c -> b = c
theorems.summary: A common left addend can be cancelled.

theorems.name: zero_le
theorems.statement: forall n. 0 <= n
theorems.summary: Zero is below every natural number.

theorems.name: le_succ_self
theorems.statement: forall n. n <= S n
theorems.summary: Every natural number is below its successor.

theorems.name: le_zero
theorems.statement: forall n. n <= 0 -> n = 0
theorems.summary: Only zero is less than or equal to zero.

theorems.name: one_le_of_ne_zero
theorems.statement: forall n. ~(n = 0) -> 1 <= n
theorems.summary: Every nonzero natural is at least one.

theorems.name: ne_zero_of_one_le
theorems.statement: forall n. 1 <= n -> ~(n = 0)
theorems.summary: A natural at least one is nonzero.

theorems.name: le_add_left
theorems.statement: forall a b. exists k. k + a = b + a
theorems.summary: Adding on the left produces an explicit order witness.

theorems.name: le_add_right
theorems.statement: forall a b. exists k. k + a = a + b
theorems.summary: Adding on the right produces an explicit order witness.

theorems.name: add_le_add_right
theorems.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + (a + c) = b + c
theorems.summary: Adding the same right summand preserves the witness-defined order.

theorems.name: add_le_add_left
theorems.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + (c + a) = c + b
theorems.summary: Adding the same left summand preserves the witness-defined order.

theorems.name: succ_le_succ
theorems.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + S a = S b
theorems.summary: Successor preserves the witness-defined order.

theorems.name: le_of_succ_le_succ
theorems.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + S a = S b) -> exists r. r + a = b
theorems.summary: Successor order reflects to the underlying naturals.

theorems.name: le_succ
theorems.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + a = S b
theorems.summary: A weak inequality remains true after raising its upper bound by one.

theorems.name: lt_to_le
theorems.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + S a = b) -> exists r. r + a = b
theorems.summary: A witnessed strict inequality entails the corresponding weak inequality.

theorems.name: add_le_cancel_right
theorems.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + (a + c) = b + c) -> exists r. r + a = b
theorems.summary: A common right summand can be cancelled from an order comparison.

theorems.name: lt_irrefl_expanded
theorems.statement: forall n. ~(exists k. k + S n = n)
theorems.summary: No natural is strictly below itself, with strict order fully expanded.

theorems.name: le_eq_or_lt
theorems.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + a = b) -> a = b \/ exists k. k + S a = b
theorems.summary: A witnessed inequality is either equality or a witnessed strict inequality.

theorems.name: lt_of_lt_of_le
theorems.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + S a = b) -> (exists k. k + b = c) -> exists k. k + S a = c
theorems.summary: Strict order followed by weak order remains strict.

theorems.name: lt_of_le_of_lt
theorems.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + a = b) -> (exists k. k + S b = c) -> exists k. k + S a = c
theorems.summary: Weak order followed by strict order remains strict.

theorems.name: lt_trans
theorems.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + S a = b) -> (exists k. k + S b = c) -> exists k. k + S a = c
theorems.summary: Strict order is transitive.

theorems.name: le_or_lt
theorems.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + a = b) \/ exists k. k + S b = a
theorems.summary: Any two naturals satisfy weak order in one direction or strict order in the other.

theorems.name: lt_trichotomy
theorems.statement: forall a b. a = b \/ ((exists k. k + S a = b) \/ exists k. k + S b = a)
theorems.summary: Two naturals are equal or strictly ordered in exactly one displayed direction.

theorems.name: lt_not_le
script: have hbad : forall z u v. ~(z = u + (v + S z))
theorems.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + S a = b) -> ~ (exists k. k + b = a)
theorems.summary: A strict inequality excludes the reverse weak inequality.

theorems.name: le_not_lt
theorems.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + a = b) -> ~ (exists k. k + S b = a)
theorems.summary: A weak inequality excludes strict inequality in the reverse direction.

theorems.name: lt_not_eq_add_middle
script: have hbad : forall z a w b. ~(z = (a + (w + S z)) + b)
theorems.statement: forall r m a b. (exists k. k + S r = m) -> ~(r = (a + m) + b)
theorems.summary: A strict upper bound prevents the lower term from containing that bound as an additive middle block.

theorems.name: mul_le_mul_left
theorems.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + c * a = c * b
theorems.summary: Left multiplication preserves the witness-defined order.

theorems.name: mul_le_mul_right
theorems.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + a * c = b * c
theorems.summary: Right multiplication preserves the witness-defined order.

theorems.name: mul_lt_mul_succ_left_nonzero
script: trans S c * a + S c
theorems.statement: forall c a. ~(c = 0) -> exists r. r + S (c * a) = c * S a
theorems.summary: Multiplication by a nonzero left factor strictly increases across a successor step.

theorems.name: division_remainder_succ
theorems.statement: forall d n. exists q r. n = S d * q + r /\ S r <= S d
theorems.summary: Every dividend has a quotient and bounded remainder for a successor divisor.

theorems.name: division_remainder_exists
theorems.statement: forall m n. ~(m = 0) -> exists q r. n = m * q + r /\ S r <= m
theorems.summary: Every positive divisor admits a quotient and a strictly bounded remainder.

theorems.name: remainder_bound_step
theorems.statement: forall r d. (exists k. k + S r = d) -> S r = d \/ exists k. k + S (S r) = d
theorems.summary: A bounded remainder either reaches the divisor or remains bounded after successor.

theorems.name: division_block_upper
theorems.statement: forall d q r. (exists k. k + S r = d) -> exists k. k + S (d * q + r) = d * S q
theorems.summary: A bounded remainder keeps its decomposition below the next divisor block.

theorems.name: positive_quotient_gap_impossible
theorems.statement: forall m q q2 r s k. (exists z. z + S r = m) -> S k + q = q2 -> ~(m * q + r = m * q2 + s)
theorems.summary: A positive gap between quotients makes two bounded-remainder decompositions unequal.

theorems.name: remainder_unique_same_quotient
theorems.statement: forall d q r s. d * q + r = d * q + s -> r = s
theorems.summary: Equal decompositions with the same quotient have equal remainders.

theorems.name: division_remainder_unique
script: have hsum : m * q + r = m * q2 + r2
theorems.statement: forall m n q r q2 r2. n = m * q + r -> (exists k. k + S r = m) -> n = m * q2 + r2 -> (exists k. k + S r2 = m) -> q = q2 /\ r = r2
theorems.summary: Bounded quotient-remainder decompositions have unique quotients and remainders.

theorems.name: zero_remainder_implies_multiple
theorems.statement: forall m n q. n = m * q + 0 -> exists k. n = m * k
theorems.summary: A quotient decomposition with zero remainder supplies a divisibility witness.

theorems.name: multiple_has_zero_remainder
theorems.statement: forall m n. ~(m = 0) -> (exists q. n = m * q) -> exists q r. (n = m * q + r /\ r = 0) /\ S r <= m
theorems.summary: Every multiple of a nonzero divisor has a bounded zero-remainder decomposition.

theorems.name: add_eq_zero_left
theorems.statement: forall a b. a + b = 0 -> a = 0
theorems.summary: A sum equal to zero has zero as its left addend.

theorems.name: add_eq_zero_components
theorems.statement: forall a b. a + b = 0 -> a = 0 /\ b = 0
theorems.summary: Both summands of a zero sum are zero.

theorems.name: mul_eq_one_components
script: have hz : S a * b + a = 0
theorems.statement: forall a b. a * b = 1 -> a = 1 /\ b = 1
theorems.summary: A product is one only when both natural factors are one.

theorems.name: mul_ne_zero
theorems.summary: A product of two nonzero naturals is nonzero.

theorems.name: mul_left_cancel_nonzero
theorems.statement: forall a b c. ~(a = 0) -> a * b = a * c -> b = c
theorems.summary: A nonzero common left factor can be cancelled.

theorems.name: mul_right_cancel_nonzero
theorems.statement: forall a b c. ~(c = 0) -> a * c = b * c -> a = b
theorems.summary: A nonzero common right factor can be cancelled.

theorems.name: two_large_factors_impossible
script: have hzero : 0 = S a * S (S b) + b
have hzero' : S a * S (S b) + b = 0
have hprod : S a * S (S b) = 0
have hz : S a = 0 \/ S (S b) = 0
theorems.statement: forall a b. ~(2 = S (S a) * S (S b))
theorems.summary: Two naturals at least two cannot multiply to two.

theorems.name: prime_two
theorems.summary: Two is prime in the expanded first-order prime predicate.

theorems.name: multiple_zero
theorems.statement: forall a. exists q. 0 = a * q
theorems.summary: Zero is a multiple of every natural number.

theorems.name: one_multiple
theorems.statement: forall n. exists q. n = 1 * q
theorems.summary: Every natural number is a multiple of one.

theorems.name: multiple_refl
theorems.statement: forall a. exists q. a = a * q
theorems.summary: Every natural number is a multiple of itself.

theorems.name: multiple_add
theorems.statement: forall a n m. (exists q. n = a * q) -> (exists r. m = a * r) -> exists s. n + m = a * s
theorems.summary: Multiples of a fixed number are closed under addition.

theorems.name: multiple_mul_right
theorems.statement: forall a n m. (exists q. n = a * q) -> exists s. n * m = a * s
theorems.summary: A right multiple of a multiple remains a multiple.

theorems.name: multiple_mul_left
script: suffices hswap : m * n = n * m
theorems.statement: forall a n m. (exists q. n = a * q) -> exists s. m * n = a * s
theorems.summary: A left multiple of a multiple remains a multiple.

theorems.name: multiple_trans
theorems.statement: forall a b n. (exists q. n = a * q) -> (exists r. a = b * r) -> exists s. n = b * s
theorems.summary: The multiple relation is transitive.

theorems.name: divisor_le_nonzero
script: have h1q : exists k. k + 1 = x
theorems.statement: forall d n. ~(n = 0) -> (exists q. n = d * q) -> exists k. k + d = n
theorems.summary: A divisor of a nonzero natural is bounded by that natural.

theorems.name: divisor_one
theorems.statement: forall d. (exists y. 1 = d * y) -> d = 1
theorems.summary: Every natural divisor of one equals one.

theorems.name: multiple_antisymm
theorems.statement: forall a b. (exists x. b = a * x) -> (exists y. a = b * y) -> a = b
theorems.summary: Mutual divisibility is antisymmetric over natural numbers.

theorems.name: factor_difference
script: have hred : c * u = c * v + r
theorems.statement: forall c u v r. c * u = c * v + r -> exists w. r = c * w
theorems.summary: A common-factor difference is itself a multiple of that factor.

theorems.name: divides_remainder
theorems.statement: forall c a b q r. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> a = b * q + r -> exists w. r = c * w
theorems.summary: A common divisor of a dividend and divisor also divides the remainder.

theorems.name: divides_linear_step
theorems.statement: forall c b q r. (exists u. b = c * u) -> (exists v. r = c * v) -> exists w. b * q + r = c * w
theorems.summary: A common divisor of a divisor and remainder divides their Euclidean linear step.

theorems.name: not_multiple_pointwise
theorems.statement: forall a n. ~(exists q. n = a * q) -> forall q. ~(n = a * q)
theorems.summary: Turn a negated existential multiple into pointwise inequalities.

theorems.name: not_multiple_from_pointwise
theorems.statement: forall a n. (forall q. ~(n = a * q)) -> ~(exists q. n = a * q)
theorems.summary: Reconstruct a negated existential from pointwise inequalities.

theorems.name: is_gcd_zero_right
theorems.statement: forall a. (((exists x. a = a * x) /\ (exists y. 0 = a * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. 0 = c * v) -> exists w. a = c * w)
theorems.summary: Every natural is the relational gcd of itself and zero.

theorems.name: is_gcd_symm
theorems.statement: forall g a b. (((exists x. a = g * x) /\ (exists y. b = g * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w) -> ((exists x. b = g * x) /\ (exists y. a = g * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. b = c * u) -> (exists v. a = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w
theorems.summary: The expanded relational greatest-common-divisor specification is symmetric.

theorems.name: is_gcd_dvd_left
theorems.statement: forall g a b. (((exists x. a = g * x) /\ (exists y. b = g * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w) -> exists x. a = g * x
theorems.summary: A relational greatest common divisor divides its left input.

theorems.name: is_gcd_dvd_right
theorems.statement: forall g a b. (((exists x. a = g * x) /\ (exists y. b = g * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w) -> exists y. b = g * y
theorems.summary: A relational greatest common divisor divides its right input.

theorems.name: is_gcd_greatest
theorems.statement: forall g a b c. (((exists x. a = g * x) /\ (exists y. b = g * y)) /\ forall d. (exists u. a = d * u) -> (exists v. b = d * v) -> exists w. g = d * w) -> (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w
theorems.summary: Every common divisor of the inputs divides their relational gcd.

theorems.name: is_gcd_of_dvd
theorems.statement: forall a b. (exists y. b = a * y) -> (((exists x. a = a * x) /\ (exists y. b = a * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. a = c * w)
theorems.summary: If the left input divides the right, the left input is their relational gcd.

theorems.name: is_gcd_unique
script: have hdg : exists w. g = h * w
have gdh : exists w. h = g * w
theorems.statement: forall g h a b. (((exists x. a = g * x) /\ (exists y. b = g * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w) -> (((exists x. a = h * x) /\ (exists y. b = h * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. h = c * w) -> g = h
theorems.summary: The fully expanded relational greatest common divisor is unique.

theorems.name: is_gcd_euclid_forward
theorems.statement: forall d a b q r. a = b * q + r -> (((exists x. b = d * x) /\ (exists y. r = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. b = c * u) -> (exists v. r = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w) -> (((exists x. a = d * x) /\ (exists y. b = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w)
theorems.summary: A relational gcd of divisor and remainder is a gcd of dividend and divisor.

theorems.name: is_gcd_euclid_backward
theorems.statement: forall d a b q r. a = b * q + r -> (((exists x. a = d * x) /\ (exists y. b = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w) -> (((exists x. b = d * x) /\ (exists y. r = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. b = c * u) -> (exists v. r = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w)
theorems.summary: A relational gcd of dividend and divisor is a gcd of divisor and remainder.

theorems.name: coprime_symm
theorems.statement: forall a b. (forall d. (exists x. a = d * x) -> (exists y. b = d * y) -> d = 1) -> forall c. (exists u. b = c * u) -> (exists v. a = c * v) -> c = 1
theorems.summary: Coprimality in its expanded common-divisor form is symmetric.

theorems.name: coprime_one_right
theorems.statement: forall a d. (exists x. a = d * x) -> (exists y. 1 = d * y) -> d = 1
theorems.summary: Every natural is coprime to one in the expanded common-divisor relation.

theorems.name: coprime_one_left
theorems.statement: forall a d. (exists x. 1 = d * x) -> (exists y. a = d * y) -> d = 1
theorems.summary: One is coprime to every natural in the expanded common-divisor relation.

theorems.name: coprime_to_is_gcd_one
theorems.statement: forall a b. (forall d. (exists x. a = d * x) -> (exists y. b = d * y) -> d = 1) -> (((exists x. a = 1 * x) /\ (exists y. b = 1 * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. 1 = c * w)
theorems.summary: Expanded coprimality constructs the relational gcd witness one.

theorems.name: is_gcd_one_to_coprime
script: have hd : exists w. 1 = c * w
theorems.statement: forall a b. (((exists x. a = 1 * x) /\ (exists y. b = 1 * y)) /\ forall d. (exists u. a = d * u) -> (exists v. b = d * v) -> exists w. 1 = d * w) -> forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> c = 1
theorems.summary: A relational gcd witness one implies expanded coprimality.

theorems.name: mod_eq_refl
theorems.statement: forall m a. exists u v. a + m * u = a + m * v
theorems.summary: Balanced natural congruence is reflexive.

theorems.name: mod_eq_symm
theorems.statement: forall m a b. (exists u v. a + m * u = b + m * v) -> exists r s. b + m * r = a + m * s
theorems.summary: Balanced natural congruence is symmetric.

theorems.name: dvd_to_mod_zero
theorems.statement: forall m a. (exists k. a = m * k) -> exists u v. a + m * u = 0 + m * v
theorems.summary: A multiple is balanced-congruent to zero.

theorems.name: add_residue
theorems.statement: forall a u c r s. r = a * c + s -> a * u + r = a * (u + c) + s
theorems.summary: Absorb a second quotient into an existing residue equation.

theorems.name: add_residue_lift
script: trans a * u + ((r + a * q) + t)
trans a * u + ((a * q + r) + t)
theorems.statement: forall a x u r q t c s. x = a * q + t -> r + t = a * c + s -> (a * u + r) + x = a * ((u + q) + c) + s
theorems.summary: Combine two quotient-and-residue summands and normalize the residue.

theorems.name: square_decomp
script: trans a * (q * z) + r * (a * q + r)
trans a * (q * z) + (r * (a * q) + r * r)
trans a * (q * z) + (a * (r * q) + r * r)
trans (a * (q * z) + a * (r * q)) + r * r
theorems.statement: forall a z q r. z = a * q + r -> z * z = a * (q * z + r * q) + r * r
theorems.summary: Expand a square while retaining an explicit quotient and remainder.

theorems.name: square_residue_lift
script: trans a * (q * z + r * q) + r * r
theorems.statement: forall a z q r c s. z = a * q + r -> r * r = a * c + s -> z * z = a * ((q * z + r * q) + c) + s
theorems.summary: Lift one quotient-and-remainder equation through squaring.

theorems.name: square_residue_witness
theorems.statement: forall a z q r c s. z = a * q + r -> r * r = a * c + s -> exists w. z * z = a * w + s
theorems.summary: Existential wrapper for the generic square-residue lift.

theorems.name: fourth_power_regroup
theorems.statement: forall n. n * n * n * n = (n * n) * (n * n)
theorems.summary: Regroup a fourth power as the square of a square.

theorems.name: mod5_residue_complete
theorems.statement: forall n. exists q. n = 5 * q \/ n = 5 * q + 1 \/ n = 5 * q + 2 \/ n = 5 * q + 3 \/ n = 5 * q + 4
theorems.summary: Every natural number has one of the five canonical residues modulo five.

theorems.name: mod5_nonzero_residue_cases
theorems.statement: forall n. ~(exists q. n = 5 * q) -> exists q. n = 5 * q + 1 \/ n = 5 * q + 2 \/ n = 5 * q + 3 \/ n = 5 * q + 4
theorems.summary: A nonmultiple of five lies in one of the four nonzero residue classes.

theorems.name: mod5_square_residue_one
theorems.statement: forall z q. z = 5 * q + 1 -> z * z = 5 * (q * z + q) + 1
theorems.summary: Squaring residue one modulo five preserves residue one.

theorems.name: mod5_square_residue_two
theorems.statement: forall z q. z = 5 * q + 2 -> z * z = 5 * ((q * z + q) + q) + 4
theorems.summary: Squaring residue two modulo five gives residue four.

theorems.name: mod5_square_residue_three
theorems.summary: Squaring residue three modulo five gives residue four.

theorems.name: mod5_square_residue_four
theorems.summary: Squaring residue four modulo five gives residue one.

theorems.name: mod5_fourth_power_residue_one
theorems.summary: A number congruent to one modulo five has fourth power congruent to one.

theorems.name: mod5_fourth_power_residue_two
theorems.summary: A number congruent to two modulo five has fourth power congruent to one.

theorems.name: mod5_fourth_power_residue_three
theorems.summary: A number congruent to three modulo five has fourth power congruent to one.

theorems.name: mod5_fourth_power_residue_four
theorems.summary: A number congruent to four modulo five has fourth power congruent to one.

theorems.name: mod5_fourth_power_one
script: have hsquare : n * n = 5 * ((x * n + 1 * x) + 0) + 1
have hsquare : n * n = 5 * ((x * n + 2 * x) + 0) + 4
have hsquare : n * n = 5 * ((x * n + 3 * x) + 1) + 4
have hsquare : n * n = 5 * ((x * n + 4 * x) + 3) + 1
theorems.statement: forall n. ~(exists x. n = 5 * x) -> exists x. n * n * n * n = 5 * x + 1
theorems.summary: A fourth power of a nonmultiple of five is one modulo five.
